title: A Bad Line from the Warehouse
gist_ar: مكالمة بتتقطع. التفاصيل ناقصة ومتكرّرة غلط — لازم تعيد تركيب الصح.

before_listening.en: The line keeps dropping and half the numbers are said twice, wrongly the first time. Reconstruct what is actually in the crate.
before_listening.ar: المكالمة بتقطع ونص الأرقام بتتقال مرتين، الأولى غلط. أعِد تركيب اللي فعلاً في الصندوق.

segments.speaker: Operations
segments.text: Karim? Karim, you're breaking up. Say the number again.

segments.speaker: Karim
segments.text: ...four one... no, hold on, that's the bay. Four one seven. Pallet four one seven. Can you—

segments.speaker: Karim
segments.text: Four ONE seven. There's a one in the middle. It's the one with the seal gone on the short side, not the top. Short side.

segments.speaker: Operations
segments.text: Short side, seal gone, four one seven. And that's the Meridian consignment.

segments.speaker: Karim
segments.text: No. No, that's the whole reason I'm ringing you. The paperwork says Meridian. The crate stencil says Volkert, and the temperature strip inside is a Volkert strip, they're the green ones with the— ...are you still there?

segments.speaker: Operations
segments.text: I'm here. Paperwork Meridian, crate Volkert. Read me the strip.

segments.speaker: Karim
segments.text: Strip's showing... it's sat at minus eighteen for most of it, then there's a window where it goes up. I want to say six hours. Could be eight, the marks are close together and this torch is— hang on— ...right, eight. Eight hours, up to minus four.

segments.speaker: Operations
segments.text: Minus four for eight hours. That's over.

segments.speaker: Karim
segments.text: It's over. And before you ask, no, I can't tell you when. The strip doesn't timestamp, it just draws. But the port stamp on the outside is the nineteenth and it landed here Tuesday, so the window's inside those five days somewhere.

segments.speaker: Karim
segments.text: Then nineteenth to twenty-third, and the eight hours is in there. There's one more thing and then I'll lose you, I've got one bar. There are two pallets with the seal gone, not one.

segments.speaker: Karim
segments.text: Four one seven and four two one. Twenty-one, not seventeen, on the second one. Same stencil, same green strip. I've only read the strip on seventeen. I'm not opening the other one on my own and without somebody from quality standing next to me, and I'd put that in writing if you want.

segments.speaker: Operations
segments.text: Don't open it. Don't touch it. Photograph both stencils, both seals, and the strip you've already read, and stay off the radio about it until I've spoken to Nadia.

segments.speaker: Karim
segments.text: Understood. Photographs, no radio, wait for Nadia. And Ops — put in your note that I said two pallets at twenty past eleven. Because if this turns into a thing, I don't want to be the man who mentioned the second one on Thursday.

gist_question.q: What is the single most important thing Karim reports?
options: That the temperature strip cannot be timestamped
That two pallets have broken seals, not one
That his torch battery is failing
That the port stamp is dated the nineteenth

questions.q: What does the temperature strip show?
options: Six hours at minus four
Eight hours at minus eighteen
A steady minus eighteen across the whole journey, with no excursion at all
Eight hours rising to minus four, within the 19th–23rd window

questions.q: Why does Karim ask Operations to note the time he called?
options: To protect himself from later being said to have raised the second pallet late
So his overtime can be calculated correctly
Because the strip readings expire after a set period
Because the quality team only works fixed hours

questions.q: What discrepancy makes Karim ring in the first place?
options: The pallet is sitting in the wrong bay, which is why he could not read the number
The seal is broken on the top rather than the short side
The paperwork says Meridian but the crate and strip are Volkert
The port stamp is missing altogether
